kept.title: Unsafe deserialization of environment lookup results
kept.description: The parse function uses JSON.parse on environment variables prefixed with a randomly generated token, potentially leading to arbitrary object injection if an attacker can control environment variable content.
steps_to_exploit: Find a target application using shell-quote with a function-based env lookup
Inject a payload into the environment environment that mimics the token-prefixed structure
Trigger the parse function
Observe arbitrary objects being injected into the output token list
kept.impact: Code execution or logic bypass in applications consuming the output tokens.

kept.title: Use of unsafe regex for tokenization
kept.description: The chunker RegExp in parse.js is built from user-controlled configuration (opts.escape) and constants, which can cause ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) if specifically crafted inputs are provided.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a long input string with repeating characters that match the BAREWORD pattern
Provide an input that forces backtracking within the regex engine
Observe the event loop blocking during parsing
kept.impact: Denial of service via resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Disabled SSL verification in CI/CD pipelines
kept.description: Several workflows explicitly set NPM_CONFIG_STRICT_SSL: false, which disables TLS verification for npm package downloads.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a Man-in-the-Middle attack on the runner network
Intercept npm traffic during the 'install' steps
Inject malicious code into the dependencies being installed
kept.impact: Compromise of build environment and potential inclusion of malicious code in the product.

kept.title: Potential Command Injection via Unsanitized Input
kept.description: The quote function uses a blacklist-based approach for quoting special characters. If new shell metacharacters are added to environments without updating this regex, command injection is possible.
steps_to_exploit: Pass input that contains shell metacharacters not covered by GLOB_SHELL_SPECIAL
Have the output evaluated by a shell
Observe unexpected command execution
kept.impact: Remote code execution if the quoted string is passed to a shell.

kept.title: Excessive privileges for automatic rebase workflow
kept.description: The rebase.yml workflow grants write access to 'contents', which is excessive and could lead to unauthorized code modifications via PR manipulation.
steps_to_exploit: Create a malicious PR against the target repository
Exploit the rebase action to push code into the branch
Use the gained write access to modify project files

evidence.quote: contents: write # for ljharb/rebase to push code to rebase

kept.title: Insecure environment configuration in workflows
kept.description: The CI pipeline installs npm packages with ignore-scripts, but then performs manual modifications to package.json via string manipulation in shell.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate the CI build environment
Observe that the package.json modification logic is fragile and could be subverted
Inject malicious dependencies into the modified package.json
kept.impact: Dependency confusion or malicious package injection.

kept.title: Insecure handling of line terminators in quotes
kept.description: The quote function throws on line terminators for glob patterns but uses inconsistent regex-based sanitization for other inputs.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a token containing line terminators outside the glob context
Observe the output string breaking the shell command context
Attempt to execute injected commands across line breaks

kept.title: Potential Prototype Pollution via env lookup
kept.description: The getVar function accesses properties directly from the env object. If a user-supplied object is passed as env, prototype pollution can occur.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a malicious env object containing properties like '__proto__'
Trigger the parse function
Verify that the global object prototype has been modified

evidence.quote: var r = typeof env === 'function' ? env(key) : env[key];

code_refs.quote: var r = typeof env === 'function' ? env(key) : env[key];

kept.title: Use of Math.random for security-sensitive tokens
kept.description: The token generator uses Math.random, which is not cryptographically secure and can be predicted, potentially allowing an attacker to guess the token used to prefix env variables.
steps_to_exploit: Monitor output to observe token generation patterns
Predict future tokens
Construct malicious environment variable values to match the predicted token
kept.impact: Bypass of the JSON deserialization security mechanism.

kept.title: Lack of rate limiting in CI actions
kept.description: The workflows allow for public PRs to trigger multiple complex build steps without restrictive rate limiting on the GitHub runners.
steps_to_exploit: Automate the submission of PRs
Exhaust repository build minutes
Force the project to pay for more CI minutes
kept.impact: Financial loss and denial of service for CI pipelines.

kept.title: Dependency risk in build scripts
kept.description: The package uses 'safe-publish-latest' and 'auto-changelog', which are dynamic build-time dependencies that can execute code during the build process.
steps_to_exploit: Compromise a minor dependency used by one of the build tools
Inject malicious code into the build process
Ensure malicious code is included in the published package

kept.title: Loose Linting Rules
kept.description: The eslint config disables many security-relevant rules, such as complexity and max-depth, making it easier for vulnerabilities to hide in complex code.
steps_to_exploit: Analyze the code for complex functions
Write bugs that are obscured by high cyclomatic complexity
Bypass code review checks because linters don't flag the complexity

kept.title: Insecure reliance on shell behavior for quoting
kept.description: The library attempts to mirror shell behavior, which is notoriously inconsistent and complex, leading to mismatches between what the library expects and what the host shell actually does.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a mismatch in shell parsing (e.g., POSIX vs bash)
Craft inputs that behave differently in the two contexts
Bypass sanitization layers

kept.title: Weak test coverage for edge cases
kept.description: Coverage config excludes 'test' and 'example' folders and sets low thresholds, allowing untested code paths that might contain vulnerabilities.
steps_to_exploit: Find functions with low coverage
Identify corner cases not covered by tests
Craft inputs to trigger vulnerabilities in those paths

kept.title: Potential denial of service via regex index manipulation
kept.description: The matchAll function manually adjusts the lastIndex property of a global regex, which can lead to infinite loops if not handled perfectly.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a specific string input that causes regex execution to fail at the expected index
Observe the infinite loop as the code tries to advance the index
Denial of service
